section_summary: This section contains diplomatic and intelligence records from 1940 to 1944 concerning Japanese naval expansion, shipbuilding capacity, and vessel operations. Key topics include investigations into Japanese naval inspection and oil purchasing activities in Los Angeles, technical data on naval vessels and private shipyards, and intelligence reports regarding battleship construction. Later documents detail reports from Chinese intelligence on a major 1944 overhaul and modernization program for Japanese submarines and surface ships assisted by German experts.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note referencing Ambassador Grew's telegram No. 106 regarding the Japanese Navy Minister's statement on naval appropriations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference file sheet indexing Tokyo telegram No. 106 regarding Japanese naval building plans and Diet statements.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on Japanese Naval Building Plans

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting the Japanese Navy Minister's statement to the Diet concerning American naval expansion under the Vinson plans.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Navy Minister's remarks that Japanese defense building programs adequately counter American naval expansion plans.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 106 from Tokyo Regarding Japanese Naval Appropriations

subfiles.about: FBI transmittal letter forwarding Special Agent Hood's report on Japanese naval subversive activities and oil purchasing in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmits an FBI report regarding Japanese oil purchasing and subversive activities in Los Angeles to the State Department.
subfiles.title: FBI Letter Regarding Japanese Oil Purchasing Office in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Investigative report on the establishment of a Japanese naval oil purchasing office at the Miyako Hotel in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Special Agent Hood reports that Commander Arito Yatsugi established an unlisted Japanese naval oil purchasing office at the Miyako Hotel.
subfiles.title: FBI Report on Japanese Oil Purchasing Office in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Letter acknowledging receipt of the FBI report on the Japanese Oil Purchasing Office in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Berle acknowledges receipt of the FBI report concerning the Japanese Oil Purchasing Office and noted distribution to military intelligence.
subfiles.title: State Department Acknowledgment of FBI Report

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting diplomatic notes and memorandum of conversation regarding Japanese naval personnel operating from Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Long informs Secretary Knox of diplomatic representations made to the Japanese Embassy regarding their naval officers in Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Secretary of the Navy Concerning Japanese Naval Inspectorate

subfiles.about: Navy Department letter reporting that Japanese naval inspectorate personnel continue to operate an office at the Miyako Hotel.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Forrestal advises State that Commander Tokuji Taira and Japanese naval personnel maintain an office at the Miyako Hotel.
subfiles.title: Navy Department Letter Regarding Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum recommending an official inquiry to the Japanese Embassy concerning unauthorized naval activities in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Coville reviews previous U.S. objections to Japanese naval inspector activities in Los Angeles and recommends sending an inquiry to the Embassy.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Formal diplomatic note requesting an explanation regarding Japanese naval inspector personnel maintaining an office in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State requests an explanation from the Japanese Embassy regarding reports of naval inspector officials operating in Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to Japanese Chargé d'Affaires

subfiles.about: Diplomatic note explaining the temporary presence of Japanese naval officers in Los Angeles for oil purchasing and transport handling.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Embassy assures the Secretary of State that no independent office exists in Los Angeles, only temporary visits for fuel purchasing.
subfiles.title: Note No. 301 from Japanese Embassy Concerning Naval Inspectorate Personnel

subfiles.about: Memorandum detailing oral explanations provided by First Secretary Yamada regarding Japanese naval officers staying at Los Angeles hotels.
subfiles.summary: Yamada explains movements of Commanders Yatsugi, Sasaki, and Taira, stating hotel stays for fueling operations do not constitute an independent office.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation Between Joseph W. Ballantine and Yoshitaro Yamada

subfiles.about: Draft note reiterating U.S. expectations that Japanese naval inspector activities conform to the policy against maintaining Los Angeles personnel.
subfiles.summary: Draft reply reminding the Japanese Embassy of American objections to extended stays of naval inspector personnel in Los Angeles.
subfiles.title: Draft Note to Japanese Chargé d'Affaires Concerning Naval Inspectorate

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter forwarding confidential intelligence concerning Japanese naval construction and industrial facilities.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmits a confidential intelligence memorandum concerning Japanese capital ship construction, naval bases, and industrial facilities to the State Department.
subfiles.title: FBI Letter Transmitting Intelligence on Japanese Naval and Industrial Facilities

subfiles.about: Intelligence memorandum detailing Japanese capital ships, submarine bases, dockyard expansions, Pacific island bases, and industrial production.
subfiles.summary: Confidential report detailing construction of battleships Kii and Owari, submarine developments, Mandate base fortifications, and industrial munition plants.
subfiles.title: Confidential Memorandum on Japanese Naval Construction and Industrial Facilities

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter forwarding intelligence regarding Japanese shipbuilding delays and production shortages.
subfiles.summary: Hoover forwards an intelligence report on Japanese shipbuilding conditions and production delays to the State Department.
subfiles.title: FBI Letter Transmitting Memorandum on Japanese Shipbuilding

subfiles.about: Intelligence report analyzing Japanese shipyard labor shortages, material scarcities, and construction delays.
subfiles.summary: Report indicates severe shortages of labor and materials doubled construction times and tripled repair durations in Japanese shipyards during 1940.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report on Japanese Shipbuilding Conditions

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter providing intelligence on Japanese naval launchings, merchant conversions, aircraft production, and shipyard installations.
subfiles.summary: Hoover transmits lists of launched warships and shipyard facilities, while reporting suspended liner construction and production of Mitsubishi MC-20 transports.
subfiles.title: FBI Letter Transmitting Intelligence on Japanese Naval Vessels and Shipyards

subfiles.about: Intelligence list cataloguing cruisers, destroyers, submarines, minesweepers, minelayers, and subchasers launched in Japan between 1937 and 1940.
subfiles.summary: Detailed tabular compilation of Japanese naval vessels launched between 1937 and 1940, including launch dates and builder shipyards.
subfiles.title: List of Japanese Naval Vessels Launched from 1937 to Summer 1940

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the tabular intelligence list of Japanese naval vessels launched between 1937 and 1940.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the intelligence list detailing Japanese cruisers, destroyers, submarines, and auxiliary craft launched from 1937 to 1940.
subfiles.title: Duplicate List of Japanese Naval Vessels Launched from 1937 to Summer 1940

subfiles.about: Technical intelligence report surveying drydocks, building berths, crane capacities, and engine facilities across Japanese shipyards.
subfiles.summary: Detailed technical survey of Japanese shipbuilding facilities, including Mitsubishi, Osaka Iron Works, Mitsui Tama, Kobe Steel, Asano, Hakodate, and Kawasaki.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report on Major Japanese Shipyards and Engineering Works

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of technical survey detailing dimensions and capacities of major Japanese shipyards and drydocks.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate technical report detailing dimensions, berths, drydocks, and machine capacities of major Japanese private and naval shipyards.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Report on Major Japanese Shipyards and Engineering Works

subfiles.about: FBI letter reporting Japanese Consulate statements in Seattle regarding the construction of 65,000-ton battleships and diplomatic relations.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports intelligence from the Japanese Consul in Seattle concerning construction of 65,000-ton battleships and doubts about war with America.
subfiles.title: FBI Letter on Japanese Battleship Construction and Seattle Consulate Intelligence

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a Bern telegram regarding German meteorological services utilizing observers aboard German and Japanese submarines.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference file sheet indexing Bern telegram No. 1360 concerning German meteorological service observers aboard German and Japanese submarines.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note on German-Japanese Submarine Meteorological Observations

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting supplementary intelligence from General Wang Peng-sheng on Japanese naval reconditioning and submarine construction.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Gauss transmits supplementary Chinese intelligence identifying converted ships Nishizono and Yura, submarine production statistics, and battleship fleet anchorages.
subfiles.title: Chungking Despatch No. 2325 on Reconditioning of Japanese Naval Vessels

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording General Wang Peng-sheng's intelligence regarding vessel identities, submarine construction figures, and battleship anchorages.
subfiles.summary: Boehringer records General Wang's clarification on converted ships Nishizono and Yura, Japanese submarine production quotas, and main fleet disposition at Ariake.
subfiles.title: Chungking Embassy Memorandum on Conference with General Wang Peng-sheng

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting Chinese intelligence report and Naval Attaché evaluation on Japanese naval reconditioning programs.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Gauss forwards General Wang's report on Japanese naval overhauls and German technical assistance, alongside the Naval Attaché's critical assessment.
subfiles.title: Chungking Despatch No. 2287 on Reconditioning of Japanese Naval Vessels

subfiles.about: Memorandum detailing Chinese intelligence on the overhaul of six surface vessels and 58 submarines with German technical assistance.
subfiles.summary: Boehringer summarizes General Wang's report of German submarine experts assisting a large Japanese naval overhaul program scheduled through May 1944.
subfiles.title: Chungking Embassy Memorandum on Japanese Naval Reconditioning Program

subfiles.about: Technical statement detailing specifications and overhaul schedules for six surface warships and 58 submarines in Japanese dockyards.
subfiles.summary: Detailed intelligence compilation listing schedules, dockyards, and technical modifications for cruisers, I-class and Ro-class submarines, and rubber-coated midget submarines undergoing overhaul.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report: Naval Vessels Being Reconditioned in Japan
